USART1 PA9 (TX, AF push-pull) / PA10 (RX, input pull-up) 115200 8N1; USART2 PA2 TX only 115200 8N1 (the simulated external device, wired PA2 -> PA10 on the breadboard); PB0 push-pull output, high while the CPU is inside USART1_IRQHandler or DMA1_Channel5_IRQHandler; PB12 / PB13 inputs with pull-up read once at reset (experiment jumpers). Boot: 'UART DMA lesson a3: USART2 TX (PA2) -> USART1 RX (PA10), 115200 8N1
' then 'RX: DMA1 ch5 circular, 32 B ring + IDLE line detection
' ('PB12 low: RX DMA in NORMAL mode, not re-armed after the first message
' or 'PB13 low: RX by interrupt, RXNE for every byte + IDLE
' with a jumper). USART1 RX is started with HAL_UARTEx_ReceiveToIdle_DMA on a 32-byte ring (DMA1 channel 5, circular, peripheral to memory): reception events are the DMA half transfer (ring position 16), transfer complete (32 = wrap) and the USART IDLE line (one frame after the last byte). USART2 sends, by DMA1 channel 7, one message every 200 ms (the first 100 ms after boot) in turn: 'hello' (5 B), 'T=23.5C H=45% P=1013hPa' (23 B), '0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCD' (40 B). The main loop sleeps in WFI; at IDLE the ISR hands the assembled message to it, which prints 'msg #<n>: <len> B [<events>] irq=<k> isr=<us> us: <text>
' (events in order, k = USART1 + DMA1 ch5 interrupts the message caused, isr = DWT cycles spent in those two handlers / 72). From a fresh start: msg #1 5 B [idle] irq=1, msg #2 23 B [ht idle] irq=2, msg #3 40 B [tc ht tc idle] irq=4 (the ring position carries over: 5, 28, 4 ...). PB13 low (RXNE + IDLE interrupts): irq = bytes + 1 (6, 24, 41) and several times the ISR time. PB12 low (DMA normal mode, not re-armed at IDLE): only msg #1 arrives, every later byte is lost.

PB0: unconnected (reception-interrupt activity output)

PB13: open (the RXNE-interrupt experiment jumper to GND is not placed)

lesson-a4-freertos.description: Lesson a4: FreeRTOS V11.1.0 (GCC/ARM_CM3 port, clang) — tasks fast (prio 3, 100 ms) and blink (prio 2, 250 ms, PA5 LED) send to a queue, a logger task (prio 1) prints every message and 1 s statistics; PB12 EXTI -> xQueueSendFromISR
lesson-a4-freertos.expect:
72 MHz, FreeRTOS-Kernel V11.1.0 (port GCC/ARM_CM3, heap_4 8 KiB, tick 1 kHz on SysTick shared with HAL_IncTick; SVC starts the first task, PendSV switches context, SysTick/PendSV at priority 15, configMAX_SYSCALL_INTERRUPT_PRIORITY 5). USART1 PA9/PA10 115200 8N1, written only by the logger task. Boot: 'FreeRTOS V11.1.0 on STM32F103C8, 72 MHz, tick 1000 Hz ', 'tasks: fast prio 3 every 100 ms, blink prio 2 every 250 ms, logger prio 1; queue 8 x 8 B ', 'heap free 5192 B, starting the scheduler ' (the pending SysTick left over from the BASEPRI-masked boot is cleared, so tick 0 = scheduler start, about 16.7 ms after the first byte). Task fast (vTaskDelayUntil 100 ms) sends {seq, tick}; task blink (vTaskDelayUntil 250 ms) toggles PA5 (LED on at 250 ms, 2 Hz square wave) and sends {seq, level, tick}; the logger (lowest priority, blocked on the 8-entry queue) prints '[] fast #' about 0.1 ms after each tick 100*n, '[] blink # LED on|off' 0.19 ms (odd n) or 1.94 ms (even n, after the fast line of the same tick) after the PA5 edge, and after every 4th blink line '[] stats: context switches, idle %, queue peak

/8, stack free fast blink logger words' (S = changes of the running task in the last second, 38 without button presses; I = idle task share of DWT->CYCCNT from the kernel run-time statistics, about 96-97 %). PB12 (pull-up, EXTI falling, NVIC priority 6): a falling edge at least 50 ms after the previously accepted one sends {seq, tick} by xQueueSendFromISR + portYIELD_FROM_ISR -> '[] button # (EXTI ISR -> queue)' about 0.2 ms later. ', 10 ms sensor start-up, then once per second: (1) scan 0x08-0x77 with HAL_I2C_IsDeviceReady (1 trial, about 115 us per NACKed probe). ' (every answering address) and the three devices are set up in turn: AT24C02 8 bytes at 0x20 read, their complement written as one page, ACK polling through the 5 ms write cycle, read back -> 'AT24C02 @0x50: page write 8 B, ready after P polls, read back ok

'; BME280 chip id 0x60 and the trimming parameters -> 'BME280 @0x76: id=0x60, calibration read
'. A device without ACK prints '<name> @0x<addr>: no ACK
' ('MPU-6050 @0x68: no ACK (0x69 answers: AD0 is high)
' when 0x69 answers instead); then 'all 3 devices ok
' or '<n> of 3 devices ok
'. (3) Every cycle the working sensors are read (BME280 forced conversion with oversampling x1, status polled every 1 ms; MPU-6050 6-byte accelerometer burst) and printed as 'read: ax=<raw> ay=<raw> az=<raw> | T=<C> C P=<hPa> hPa H=<%> %

lesson-a8-nobusy.description: Lesson a8 mistake: hal-w25q without the BUSY polling — the page program is sent during the 45 ms sector erase and the read back follows at once: the flash ignores the program, the page reads FF, 'w25q FAILED'

Same as hal-w25q (72 MHz, SPI1 mode 0 at 9 MHz on PA5 SCK / PA6 MISO / PA7 MOSI, PA4 = CS, USART1 PA9 115200 8N1) without the two BUSY waits: 'W25Q32 test (SPI1 9 MHz mode 0, CS PA4)
', 'JEDEC ID EF 40 16
', 'SR1 0x00
', 'before: <16 bytes at 0x001000>
', then 06h + 20h 001000h and at once 'sector erase: sent, BUSY not polled
', 06h + 02h with 64 bytes (i * 3 + 1) while the erase is still running (tSE 45 ms) -> 'page program 64 bytes: sent, BUSY not polled
